record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: In the same computational problem for the expressiveness indicators m_i^A, determine for which families of binary column sets A one can approximate the probability P((m_i(x)=m_i(y)) for all i) when x and y are sampled uniformly at random.

evidence.quote: Computational Problem. Given A, let x and y be sampled uniformly at random. Compute: P ((mi(x) = mi(y)) ∀i)
Open Problem 2.4. For which choices of A can we approximate answers to Computational Problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n and t be positive integers, and let A = {a_1, ..., a_k} ⊂ {0,1}^n be a finite collection of binary column vectors of length n. For an n×t binary matrix x ∈ {0,1}^{n×t} and each i ∈ {1, ..., k}, define the expressiveness indicator

  m_i^A(x) = #{ j ∈ {1, ..., t} : the j-th column of x equals a_i },

i.e. the number of columns of x that coincide with the i-th element of A. Sample x and y independently and uniformly at random from {0,1}^{n×t}, and consider the probability

  P_A(n, t) = Pr[ m_i^A(x) = m_i^A(y) for every i = 1, ..., k ].

Identify those families A ⊂ {0,1}^n (or infinite families of such collections, parametrized by n and t) for which the quantity P_A(n, t) admits an efficient approximation algorithm: namely, give an algorithm that, on input (A, n, t, ε), outputs a value P̂ with |P̂ − P_A(n, t)| ≤ ε in time polynomial in n, t, |A|, and 1/ε. Characterize the structural conditions on A under which such approximations are possible.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as Open Problem 2.4 in a 2023 collection of seven open problems in applied combinatorics, asking for which families A of binary columns the associated probability can be approximated. No subsequent publication addressing this approximation question was found in web searches, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: The paper poses, among its seven problems, an open question about approximating the probability that the expressiveness indicators agree on uniformly random inputs.
